dedupe_keys.name: pruhonice ionospheric station data institute of atmospheric physics czech academy of sciences

description: The Průhonice ionospheric station of the Institute of Atmospheric Physics near Prague has sounded the ionosphere since 1957, first with a Soviet AIS ionosonde, from 1984 with an Australian IPS-42 and since January 2004 with a Digisonde DPS-4D, whose data is shown on the institute's web page in real time. It runs routine vertical sounding every 15 minutes with campaigns of more frequent soundings, plasma drift measurements for the F and E regions every 15 minutes, and synchronised oblique soundings between European observatories that can detect travelling ionospheric disturbances. The institute runs the Regional Warning Centre Prague of the International Space Environment Service (ISES), supplying daily ionospheric observations, and sends Digisonde data in real time to the European DIAS server, the global GIRO Digisonde database (with a mirror at the institute) and the SWACI European TEC maps. A transmitter of the Czech Doppler sounding system and a GNSS receiver feeding the Czech geodetic network are also at the station. Access to the real-time ionograms is free online; no licence is stated on the page read. Caveats: archives are reached through the international servers named, not a download page. Coverage is the ionosphere over the Czech Republic, with oblique paths across Europe. It supports hazard exposure analysis of space weather effects on HF communications and GNSS; related records are the NIGGG real-time geophysical data and the LAMP space weather data.
